title: Nasdaq 100 posts worst week since March 2020
body: U.S. stocks closed sharply lower Friday, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 5.61% on the day and 10.43% for the week, its worst since March 2020. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28%, wiping out its gains for the year, while the S&P 500 dropped 3.70% for its seventh straight decline. The Dow lost 950 points. Nvidia fell 14.01% to $125.53 after Reuters reported that the SEC was probing its accounting. The selling reached across the AI trade, from the companies designing chips to the ones supplying memory, optical gear and power. Treasuries caught a bid, with the 10-year yield down 12 basis points to 4.93%. Even with yields moving lower, tech shares remained under pressure. U.S. closing levels Dow Industrial Average −950.10 points (−1.93%) to 48,151.82. Week −8.03%. S&P 500 −265.44 points (−3.70%) to 6,910.39. Week −8.61%. Nasdaq Composite −1,261.47 points (−5.28%) to 22,617.73. Week −10.02%. Russell 2000 −73.32 points (−2.76%) to 2,581.79. Week −7.48%. Nasdaq 100 −1,488.07 points (−5.61%) to 25,028.98. Week −10.43%. The Dow had its worst week since March 2020. The Nasdaq Composite's 10.02% loss was in line with its worst week in the spring 2025 selloff, while the S&P 500 had its worst week since that stretch. Friday's breadth showed how far the selling spread. Nearly five Nasdaq stocks fell for every one that rose, and S&P 500 decliners outnumbered advancers 357 to 125.
